{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Interface Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — findings, walk-away items and next steps

---

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4. The agreement is workable in structure, and several of our most important commercial freedoms are already protected: the licence is expressly non-exclusive, we are affirmatively free to build or buy competing systems, there is no exclusivity, non-compete, employee non-solicit, MFN or audit right binding us, no liquidated damages or shortfall penalty, and the renewal mechanic (one-year terms, 30 days' non-renewal notice, mutual) and California law/venue both sit within acceptable limits.

The risk is concentrated in the risk-allocation articles, where the document is materially one-sided against us:

- **No Vendor IP indemnity.** Section 12(b) gives us only a breach-of-contract indemnity from TrueLink; there is no indemnity anywhere for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents or wilful misconduct, while our indemnity in 12(a) is broad. This fails even the fallback.
- **Asymmetric liability cap.** The only limitation caps TrueLink alone at 12 months' hosting/support compensation while our liability — including the broad 12(a) indemnity — is entirely uncapped. That is expressly walk-away territory under our playbook. There is also no exclusion of indirect or consequential damages anywhere, and the vendor-side cap is drafted against "Section 3, 4, 7 and 11", none of which appear as headings, leaving even that cap of uncertain scope.
- **One-way IP ownership.** Section 2(d) confirms TrueLink retains the Interface; nothing affirms that we retain rights in Client Content, our IP or our borrower/loan data, and nothing addresses ownership of the Support Services results we pay for.
- **No performance warranty.** The only TrueLink warranty is a Y2K date-processing warranty. Combined with the implied-warranty disclaimer, the practical result approaches an "AS IS" position.
- **No exit clause and no insurance.** There is no transition assistance, data return, export or deletion obligation, and no insurance covenant at all — despite TrueLink hosting our Web Site and transmitting and archiving borrower credit data from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian.

We have also flagged licence scope (no affiliates or contractors) and assignment (no successor/M&A carve-out, unqualified consent) as high-severity deviations requiring narrow edits.

Three findings carry a failed deterministic check but are substantively compliant on the text (termination for convenience, audit, non-solicit) and are recommended for reviewer waiver rather than redline — editing a clause that already meets our preferred position would only reopen favourable terms.

Separately, the fee blanks (Section 5(a) minimum monthly fee; Section 4 support period) must be completed before signature, and there are two mis-cross-references to clean up (Section 13's reference to "Section 12" for termination; Section 6's reference to minimums "listed in Section 4").

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Only a breach-of-contract indemnity from TrueLink; no IP infringement, breach of law, data incident or wilful misconduct indemnity anywhere. Add standard supplier indemnity with notice/control/cooperation procedure. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Ownership runs one way to TrueLink; no reservation of Client Content, Client IP or our data, and no ownership of Support Services results. Add Client ownership subsection at § 2(e) with licence back to embedded TrueLink IP. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | TrueLink capped at 12 months' compensation; our liability uncapped. No indirect-damages exclusion. Make cap mutual and Agreement-wide, add floor, exclude indirect damages, carve out indemnities/confidentiality/gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud/IP. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 15 is mutual with an affiliate carve-out but has no successor/M&A carve-out and an unqualified consent standard. Add successor carve-out, reasonableness standard, and bar transfer by TrueLink to a Client competitor. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Grant runs to Client alone; no affiliates or contractors and no notice mechanic to add them. Extend grant to affiliates/contractors and permit transfer to an M&A successor via § 15. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; § 2(a) expressly confirms we are not obligated to use the licence and may acquire or build similar systems. No redline. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No liquidated damages, penalty or fixed-sum remedy payable by Client; no early-termination fee. Blank minimum monthly fees noted for completion. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us; the referenced Non-Competition Agreement limits TrueLink's use of Credit Data. No redline. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Needs review (waiver recommended) | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Substantively compliant at preferred: § 14 gives an unqualified Client election to terminate, ~30–60 days' run-off, no termination fee, no Vendor convenience exit, 1-year term. Failed keyword check only — recommend reviewer waiver, no edit. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (waiver recommended) | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No audit, inspection or records-examination right against us anywhere; information flows run in our favour (§ 6 charge documentation, § 2.e usage statistics and logs). Failed check is an artefact of the absence of any audit clause. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | California law with exclusive venue in San Luis Obispo County; sits at the fallback and is accepted. No arbitration provision. Venue convenience noted only. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | The only MFN runs in our favour (§ 6 rate assurance plus one-year price freeze). No reciprocal obligation on us. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Compliant (at fallback) | § 5 COMPENSATION. | § 5(a) monthly floor sits at the fallback: exposure confined to the 12-month term, stand-alone § 14 exit, and no shortfall or acceleration mechanic. Blanks and § 6 mis-cross-reference noted. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (waiver recommended) | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No employee non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant on us — the preferred outcome. Failed checks test fallback wording of a clause that does not exist. Do not volunteer a mutual non-solicit. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | One-year initial term, successive one-year renewals, mutual 30-day non-renewal notice — meets preferred. No renewal reminder and no uplift cap, noted as minor sub-elements only. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No transition, migration, export, return or deletion obligation; § 14 only continues service to month-end and § 13 places the migration burden on us. Insert transition assistance, machine-readable data return within 30 days and certified deletion into § 14 (survives under § 24). |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only a Y2K warranty from TrueLink; no professional/workmanlike, conformance, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty and no remedy, while § 8 imposes such warranties on us. Add express warranty with repair/replace/refund remedy to § 9. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance covenant anywhere, despite TrueLink hosting Client Content and transmitting/archiving borrower Credit Data. Insert new Section 31 with CGL, E&O and cyber cover plus certificates on request. |

---

## Walk-away items

These are the points our playbook treats as walk-away territory. They must be resolved before we can recommend signature.

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped Vendor liability (§ 12).** Our liability — including the broad 12(a) indemnity covering any breach, any Client Content claim and product/service injury claims — is entirely uncapped, while TrueLink is capped at 12 months' hosting and support compensation. This is expressly identified in the rule as walk-away ("Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped"). The minimum acceptable outcome is a mutual 12-month fees cap with indemnity, confidentiality/data security and gross negligence carve-outs.
2. **No insurance from a vendor processing personal financial data.** TrueLink hosts the Web Site, receives and uploads Client Content (§ 1.b) and transmits and archives borrower and applicant credit data from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian (§ 1.d) with no insurance obligation at all. A vendor processing personal financial data with no insurance is walk-away territory, and the gap is not cured elsewhere: the § 12.b indemnity is unsupported by any coverage requirement and the vendor-side cap leaves us with no funded backstop for a data incident.
3. **Effective "AS IS" delivery (§ 9 / § 12).** The implied-warranty disclaimer is carved back "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT", but with no express performance warranty to carve out, the practical result approaches the walk-away "AS IS" position. We need at minimum the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies).
4. **Absence of any Vendor IP indemnity.** No indemnity for third-party infringement claims relating to the Interface or the Hosting/Support Services fails even the fallback, leaving us exposed on technology we do not own and cannot control.

---

## Next steps

**Redlines to issue (critical and high, in order of priority)**

1. **§ 12 — Liability.** Make the cap mutual and Agreement-wide at the greater of 12 months' compensation and USD 1,000,000; exclude indirect and consequential damages; place indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap; preserve Client payment obligations outside the limitation. Fallback: straight mutual 12-month fees cap with indemnity/confidentiality/gross negligence carve-outs.
2. **§ 12 — Indemnity.** Add a TrueLink indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data/security incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with the usual notice, control and cooperation procedure. We are not narrowing our § 12(a) indemnity in this pass, as it is largely tied to Client Content and our own web site.
3. **§ 2 — Ownership.** Insert a Client ownership subsection at § 2(e) reserving Client Content, Client IP and our data, assigning Support Services work product to us, and licensing back any embedded TrueLink IP. Fallback: perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables.
4. **§ 9 — Warranty.** Add an express performance and conformance warranty (12 months software; professional and workmanlike services) with a repair/replace/refund remedy. Fallback: 90 days software / 30 days services.
5. **§ 14 — Exit.** Insert up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Client Content and Credit Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and deletion with written certification. Fallback: 90 days' assistance. Placement in § 14 is effective post-termination because § 24 provides that Sections 1 and 5 through 30 survive.
6. **New § 31 — Insurance.** CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request. Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.
7. **§ 2 and § 15 — Licence scope and assignment.** Extend the licence to Client affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf; add an affiliate/successor carve-out for Client assignment, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard on consent, and a bar on TrueLink transferring the Agreement to a Client competitor, preserving the existing mutual structure.

**Reviewer waivers to record (no redline)**

8. Waive the failed deterministic checks on **T4C**, **AUDIT** and **NOSOLICIT** as phrasing variants or artefacts of clause absence. Each is substantively compliant, in each case because the silence or functional drafting favours us, and editing would reopen favourable terms. Under the playbook a clause meeting preferred is not redlined.

**Commercial and drafting cleanup before signature**

9. Complete the **§ 5(a) minimum monthly fee** blank and the **§ 4 support period** blank ("not less than ____ months"), confirming the minimum aligns with the one-month termination runway; an unfilled or long support period could be argued to qualify our § 14 exit as to Support Services.
10. Correct the mis-cross-references: **§ 13** points to "Section 12" for termination when termination is § 14 and § 12 is the indemnity; **§ 6** refers to minimum monthly fees "listed in Section 4" when they sit in § 5(a); and confirm that § 14's "Subject to Section 4" preserves TrueLink's support-availability period rather than qualifying our termination right. Raise if these articles are opened for other reasons.
11. Confirm the scope of the vendor-side cap's reference to "Section 3, 4, 7 and 11", none of which appear as headings in the document.

**Diligence outside this document**

12. Obtain and review the separate **Non-Competition Agreement** referenced at § 8(d). In this document it operates only as a limitation on TrueLink's licensed use of Credit Data, but we should confirm it contains no reciprocal restraint or employee non-solicit binding us.
13. Low-priority ask: raise a **renewal uplift cap** (CPI or 3%) alongside the fee schedule negotiation — § 6 freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year only, leaving renewal uplift uncapped."}
